test a simple mean combination to see if averaging improves over weighted due to high trend dominance and moderate stability.

I will test a weighted combination using the inverse_error weight (w1) to see if a simple error‑based weighting outperforms the softmax and softmax_neg_error approaches; this explores a different weight type.
Testing a median combination (trend dominated, moderate stability) to see if robust central tendency improves over weighted.
The series has strong trend and moderate seasonality; a DBA on a reduced, stable pool may capture trend dominance better than weighted mean.
Try a weighted combination on the smaller, more stable pool4 using inverse_error weights to see if a simpler, more focused weighting beats DBA.
test a per‑model softmax weighting on the trend‑dominated pool4 to see if non‑linear weighting beats DBA.
The series has moderate stability and strong trend; a per‑horizon weighted mean may capture changing strengths.
Try a DBA combination on the full pool to see if a more flexible DBA improves over the current best weighted pool4.

The series is trend-dominated with moderate stability, so a weighted mix of the strong trend models in pool4 may still be best. We will try a forward‑selection weight on pool4 to see if it outperforms the current weighted/DBA leader.
